done_when: The worker brief lets a worker update any existing test its intended change breaks, outside its scope, naming each changed test and why in its handoff; the review brief no longer reports such test files as outside scope but reports a test weakened to hide a real defect as a P1; tests through forge work and forge close show both

findings.body: The extension allowlist still excludes existing tests such as `tests/check_api.mjs`, `tests/check_api.cjs`, or `tests/test_api.sh`. None matches the filename patterns above, so an intended change updating these tests still lists them outside scope. The worker already recognizes these test-folder paths through `TEST_PATHS` in `src/forge/worker.py:23–25`. This leaves the acceptance criterion covering any existing test incomplete. Extend recognition and cover these cases through `forge close`.
findings.title: Not done: Existing tests with other extensions still appear outside scope

findings.body: The fix-brief assertions check isolated words without checking that permission is granted. Changing the fix-specific instruction to `You must not update an existing test your intended change breaks` while retaining its scope and handoff text leaves every assertion passing. The stronger assertions below inspect only the separate task brief. Assert the permission, outside-scope exception, and handoff requirement together in the fix prompt returned through `forge work`, so reversing that permission fails this test.
findings.title: Not done: forge work test enforces permission in the fix brief

why: Workers stop to ask before updating an existing test their intended change breaks, because the test file is outside the task's scope; it happened seven times on 2026-09-28
